title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 747–748): M is a profinite 'T-L-group' (a profinite group with a distinguished family of procyclic 'loop' subgroups L_i ≅ Ẑ). It carries an intrinsic 'cyclotomic' or structural character χ_M : M → Ẑ*, through which the normaliser N(L) acts on L by σ l σ^{-1} = l^{χ(σ)}. The working hypothesis is that χ_M has open image. The model is the outer Galois action on the fundamental groups of the Teichmüller tower, with L the inertia (cusp) subgroups.

On p.747 Grothendieck deduces (19): every open subgroup of N(L)/L acts non-trivially on L. He then announces a consequence obtained 'by the standard arguments'. This page states it. Let K be a field (an extension of a field of finite type over Q). Let G be an affine group scheme of finite type over K, and u : M → G(K) (20) a homomorphism. Then u|_L is 'quasi-unipotent' (21): there is an open subgroup L' ⊂ L with u(L') consisting of unipotent elements. If l_i is a generator of L = L_i, this is equivalent to (22): u(l_i) is quasi-unipotent, i.e. some power u(l_i)^n with n ≥ 1 is unipotent.

The standard argument is Grothendieck's ℓ-adic monodromy argument (Serre–Tate appendix; SGA 7 I). An open subgroup of Ẑ* contains rational integers a ≥ 2. Choose σ ∈ N(L) with χ(σ) = a. Then u(l) is conjugate to u(l)^a, so the finite set of eigenvalues of u(l) (in a faithful representation) is stable under λ ↦ λ^a. Hence every eigenvalue is a root of unity, and a power of u(l) is unipotent.

The page serves as a preliminary for p.748 (§30), on 'schematic envelopes' of a profinite T-L-group. There one takes a discretification π_0 ⊂ π, Q-group schemes G_Q, adelic points G(A_Q) ⊂ ∏ G(Q_ℓ), and 'admissible' envelopes, presumably those in which the loops map to quasi-unipotent or unipotent elements.
errors: (22) as transcribed says 'l_i^n soit unipotent'; it must be u(l_i)^n (a slip of the pen or of the transcription).

The equivalence (21) ⇔ (22) via a single generator l_i is immediate only if u is continuous for some topology on G(K) (e.g. ℓ-adic). For an abstract homomorphism, u(L) is not determined by u(l_i). The gap can be repaired: the conjugation argument applies to every x ∈ L. Moreover, for K finitely generated over Q, the roots of unity of bounded degree over K form a finite set, which gives a uniform n with u(x)^n unipotent for all x ∈ L. Since nẐ is open, (21) follows. This plausibly explains why the hypothesis 'K of finite type over Q' appears on p.747, but Grothendieck does not spell it out.

ideas.what: Quasi-unipotence of the images of loop (inertia-like) subgroups under any homomorphism to an algebraic group, deduced purely from the cyclotomic action of the normaliser with open image
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's ℓ-adic monodromy theorem (quasi-unipotence), abstracted to profinite groups with cyclotomic character
ideas.where_published: Serre–Tate, 'Good reduction of abelian varieties' (1968), appendix; SGA 7 I

ideas.what: Intrinsic cyclotomic character χ_M of an abstract profinite loop group M, with openness of its image as an axiom
ideas.modern_name: cyclotomic character on (outer) Galois / Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type groups; 'group-theoretic cyclotomic character' in anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Deligne, Drinfeld; later Mochizuki for intrinsic reconstruction
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche discuss the Teichmüller tower and Galois action; this formalism is not published as such

ideas.what: Planned use (next page) of quasi-unipotence to define admissible 'schematic envelopes' of profinite loop groups via discretifications and adelic points
ideas.modern_name: relative / weighted completion; Malcev and pro-algebraic completions

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, abstractly for profinite loop groups with cyclotomic character, the quasi-unipotence of loop images as the input for algebraic (adelic) envelopes. This anticipates the role quasi-unipotence and the cyclotomic weight play in Hain–Matsumoto's weighted completion of Galois actions on mapping class groups.
missed.quote: la restriction de u à L est "quasi-unipotente"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows an early, purely group-theoretic formulation linking monodromy quasi-unipotence to algebraic envelopes of Teichmüller-type groups. This is of historical interest for the genealogy of weighted and relative completion, though the result itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is the standard monodromy quasi-unipotence argument transplanted to an axiomatic setting. The only mildly interesting aspect is the axiomatic framework and its use toward envelope constructions on the next page.
transcription_corrections: (22): 'tel que l_i^n soit unipotent' should read 'tel que u(l_i)^n soit unipotent' (check the image; at minimum the meaning requires u).
'— ce qui revient à (21)' likely reads '— ce qui revient [à dire], si l_i est un générateur de L = L_i, que soit (22)…'; the reference back to (21) is redundant.
